messages.subject: change in occurrence distribution
parts:
Hi Chris,

We have movement data from some birds that were captive reared and released into the wild. As expected, they did not exhibit range residency, and were still expanding their space use when the tracking devices ran out. We are interested in quantifying their exploration of the landscape over the tracking period, to understand change in space use over time. I was thinking about splitting their tracks into weekly periods, and estimating an occurrence distribution for each period in ctmm to get an estimate of area used in each week. Is this is a legitimate approach?


I understand that these occurrence distributions do not represent an extrapolated home range area, and are sampling dependent. As such, do you think we need to use a random sample of the same size for each bird in each tracking period to try to control for potential sampling bias?

 

Thank you very much!

Jenny

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: change in occurrence distribution
parts:
Hi Jenny,

I would look at how their diffusion rates change over time. The diffusion rate is the increase in area per unit time.

I haven't yet gotten around to make this convenient in the package, but if you fit a BM our IOU model, then the FIT$sigma slot is the diffusion matrix. Here's some opaque code to return diffusion rate CIs in km^2/day:

# FIT must be BM or IOU: CTMM=ctmm(range=FALSE) in ctmm.guess
diffusion <- function(FIT,level=0.95,units=TRUE)
{
  FIT$range <- TRUE
  DIFF <- ctmm:::area.covm(FIT$sigma)
  DOF <- 2*ctmm:::DOF.area(FIT)
  DIFF <- ctmm:::chisq.ci(DIFF,DOF=DOF,level=level)
  if(units) { DIFF <- "km^2" %#% DIFF %#% "day" } # otherwise SI units of m^2/s
  return(DIFF)
}

Note: I ran across a bug in ctmm.fit for the IOU model and the fix is now on GitHub, which you can install via devtools::install_github("ctmm-initiative/ctmm") . So please update the package first, before attempting to run this.

Best,
Chris
